correctness.rationale: The claim is an existence theorem with two explicit positive normalized probability vectors. Strict majorization and strict convexity prove noncrossing for every real m>1. Six exact rational margins show Q above P at coverage C_P(2) and P above Q at C_P(11). Both coverages lie above both one-individual base coverages. Continuity and strict monotonicity force a crossing. The same inequalities hold for polygonal interpolation of integer sampling points; a reproducible exact-rational checker independently evaluates the fractions and direct multinomial expectations. Unproved: uniqueness of the crossing and claims for sampled estimates.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The prior claim would imply no equal-coverage crossing because this example has no size-based crossing for any m>1, by strict majorization. Yet two exact rational equal-coverage comparisons have opposite strict rankings, forcing a crossing. Therefore the source statement does not cover this result as a valid corollary: the result refutes it. The source conditions do not exclude equally rich three-species communities.

originality.rationale: The primary source Chao–Jost 2012, including complete Appendices G and H, was inspected at theorem/assumption level. Its unconditional Theorem G1 and G3 directly assert the opposite implication, and its main text repeats the statement. No prior verified counterexample with these three-species distributions or an implying general result was found in dedicated literature and research searches; nearest indexed species-discovery covariance result is strictly different. A correction buried in unindexed literature is residual risk.
residual_risks: A published correction or known counterexample outside searchable material could predate this construction; negative search alone does not establish global priority.
The 2000 Lande–DeVries–Walla full text was not available; only its publisher abstract was inspected, and it cannot be claimed fully noncovering from abstract alone.

The result is specific to theoretical expected curves under iid with-replacement sampling and standard monotone continuous/polygonal interpolation; alternate estimation and sampling conventions need separate treatment.

value.rationale: The counterexample invalidates a specific universal theoretical assertion in a foundational ecological-sampling reference about preserving qualitative species-richness rankings under a change from equal sample size to equal coverage. Equal true richness, only three species per community, and strict majorization isolate a structural phenomenon rather than sampling noise or different species counts. Exact rational certificates enable immediate reuse and verification. It does not imply coverage-based rarefaction generally lacks empirical utility.
